financials_interim.notes: Company (holding-company) basis. Company revenue (597,120,636) equals the 'Holding' column value in the Group segmental note (pg.10), confirming this is the parent entity's own management-fee/EPC-type revenue, not a subsidiary. tax_expense = Income Tax Expenses (19,436,884) + Dividend Tax (14,270,723) = 33,707,607, reconciling exactly: 261,431,528 - 33,707,607 = 227,723,921 = printed PAT. EPS 0.17 = 227,723,921 / 1,354,506,111 weighted average shares, matches printed. short_term_borrowings = Interest Bearing Loans & Borrowings, current (1,640,814,479) + Bank Overdraft (2,382,605) = 1,643,197,084; long_term_borrowings = 0 (Company non-current Interest Bearing Loans & Borrowings line is nil at both 30.06.2026 and 31.03.2026). capex = 'Acquisition of Property, Plant & Equipment' (11,158,020) only -- Company-level investing cash flow is dominated by a Rs.1,381,000,000 investment in subsidiaries (not treated as capex here) and short-term fixed-deposit movements.

Group basis. profit_before_tax = 'Profit before Taxation' (1,078,101,868), which already includes Share of results of equity accounted investee (176,591,855) on top of 'Profit from Ordinary Activities before taxation' (901,510,013). tax_expense = Income Tax Expenses (189,224,558) + Dividend Tax (14,270,723) = 203,495,281 (combined, since both are deducted to reach PAT) -- reconciles exactly: 1,078,101,868 - 203,495,281 = 874,606,587 = printed 'Profit after Taxation'. EPS 0.56 = 762,249,163 (net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders per note 5, pg.11) / 1,354,506,111 weighted average shares -- matches printed EPS exactly. shares_in_issue uses the period-end share count from the NAV note (pg.11): 1,354,667,889 (differs slightly from the EPS weighted-average count of 1,354,506,111 due to in-period share issuance -- 'Issue of Share Capital' of 11,862,050 appears in the statement of changes in equity, pg.6). short_term_borrowings = Interest Bearing Loans & Borrowings, current (1,861,360,381) + Bank Overdraft (32,951,023) = 1,894,311,404; long_term_borrowings = Interest Bearing Loans & Borrowings, non-current, only (20,419,578,835) -- Lease Liabilities (current 9,933,300 + non-current 313,652,743) excluded as a separately labelled line. capex = 'Acquisition of Property, Plant & Equipment' only (7,568,921,055) -- no separate intangible asset acquisition line in this filing; this single capex line is unusually large this quarter (vs 433,114,203 a year earlier) reflecting the ongoing BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) build-out across 13 sites disclosed in the MD's message (pg.2). total_liabilities uses the segmental note's independently-stated Group total (25,410,021,383, pg.10) rather than summing Total Non-Current Liabilities (22,559,174,137) + Total Current Liabilities (2,850,847,246) = 25,410,021,383 from the balance sheet, which match exactly -- both sources agree. cash_from_operations is sharply negative this quarter (-6,820,472,146, vs -711,359,020 prior year) almost entirely due to a Rs.8,682,342,791 increase in trade & other receivables ('Project Advances & Other Receivables' on the balance sheet rose from 1,674,648,990 to 9,792,209,995), consistent with cash advances made for the BESS project construction -- a working-capital, not profitability, item.

thesis.thesis_text: WindForce PLC is a diversified Sri Lankan renewable energy IPP spanning Wind, Solar, Hydro and a newly-built 130MW/520MWh BESS across 13 sites. In Q1 FY2026/27, Group Revenue grew 23.3% YoY to Rs.2,620.12mn, led by 41% growth in Solar generation, but PAT grew only 5.1% to Rs.874.61mn as Direct Cost (+43%) and net finance cost (+44%, to Rs.314.5mn) outpaced revenue during an active capex cycle funding the BESS build-out. A specific, quantified Rs.88.6mn Wind-segment curtailment loss from Cyclone Ditwah is being pursued for recovery from the utility under the SPPA. At Rs.38.90, the stock trades on a run-rate P/E of ~17.4x and P/B of ~1.64x, with a consistent Rs.1.00 DPS yielding ~2.6% -- not cheap, but supported by genuine capacity and revenue-stream diversification (Q1 FY2026/27 interim, source_doc_id manual_18f53e0ce7c6f2e3).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/energy-policy data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). This is WIND's first interim financial_statements entry -- no prior quarter for QoQ comparison and no annual report reviewed, though two years of dividend history (FY2024/FY2025) partially offset the single-quarter limitation. The P/E cited is a run-rate approximation (single quarter's EPS x4), not a trailing-twelve-month figure. The MD's letter and the accounting segmental note disclose different technology-level revenue splits for Solar and Hydro (though they agree on Group totals and on Wind) -- the MD's self-consistent figures are used here, per interim_updates.

financial_quality.rationale: Group Q1 FY2026/27 PAT of Rs.874.61mn on Revenue of Rs.2,620.12mn implies a run-rate ROE of approximately 10.9% (annualized PAT ~Rs.3,498.4mn / total equity Rs.32,082.16mn) -- a single-quarter approximation. Operating margin compressed to 42.5% from 47.7% YoY and net margin to 33.4% from 39.2%, as Direct Cost (+43% YoY) and net finance cost (+44% YoY, to Rs.314.5mn) both outpaced 23.3% revenue growth. Long-term borrowings of Rs.20,419.58mn against total equity of Rs.32,082.16mn (debt/equity ~0.70x including short-term borrowings) reflect a capital-intensive IPP funding an active BESS build-out; operating cash flow was sharply negative this quarter (-Rs.6,820.47mn) due to a Rs.8,682.3mn rise in project advances/receivables tied to BESS construction, a working-capital rather than profitability signal.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Revenue +23.3% YoY (Rs.2,620.12mn vs Rs.2,124.00mn) but PAT grew only 5.1% YoY (Rs.874.61mn vs Rs.832.27mn) as costs from the ongoing capex cycle outpaced revenue. Solar generation revenue was the standout, +41% YoY to Rs.813mn per the MD's letter; Wind revenue fell 4% YoY to Rs.935mn, explicitly attributed to a quantified one-off (Rs.88.6mn curtailment loss from Cyclone Ditwah-related force majeure, with recovery discussions underway under the SPPA). The new BESS segment (130MW/520MWh across 13 sites, all now installed) already contributed Rs.149.2mn of revenue ahead of full commissioning -- a concrete forward growth driver not yet fully reflected in this quarter's results.

valuation.rationale: At price Rs.38.90 (as of 2026-08-28), run-rate annualized EPS of ~Rs.2.24 (quarterly Group EPS 0.56 x4, an approximation) implies a P/E of ~17.4x. Market cap of Rs.52,718.35mn against Group total equity of Rs.32,082.16mn implies a P/B of ~1.64x. Dividend per share was Rs.1.00 in both FY2025 and FY2024 (yield ~2.6% at the current price), a consistent but modest payout for a company mid-capex-cycle. These multiples are not statistically cheap and reflect a growth premium for the BESS/renewables buildout rather than a value opportunity.

business_quality.rationale: WindForce is a diversified renewable energy IPP with generation across Wind, Solar and Hydro, plus a newly commissioned 130MW/520MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) across 13 sites -- meaningful technology and revenue-stream diversification versus a single-technology generator. Revenue is underpinned by Standardised Power Purchase Agreements (SPPA) with the national utility, and the company discloses specific, quantified operational detail (e.g. the Rs.88.6mn Cyclone Ditwah curtailment loss and its recovery process) rather than opaque aggregate figures, reflecting reasonably transparent disclosure for a Sri Lankan utility.

governance_risk.rationale: WindForce has paid a consistent Rs.1.00 DPS in both FY2024 and FY2025 (FY2023 not on file, a gap), a positive continuity signal. The company proactively discloses and quantifies a one-off adverse event (Rs.88.6mn Wind curtailment loss from Cyclone Ditwah force majeure) and its planned recovery route, rather than burying it -- a governance positive -- though this project has no circulars/disclosures feed to independently verify board or ownership changes.

key_reasons: Revenue grew 23.3% YoY to Rs.2,620.12mn, with Solar generation (+41% YoY to Rs.813mn) the standout growth driver and a new BESS segment already contributing Rs.149.2mn ahead of full commissioning
PAT growth (5.1% YoY) lagged well behind revenue growth as Direct Cost (+43%) and net finance cost (+44%, to Rs.314.5mn) both outpaced the top line during an active capex cycle
Run-rate P/E of ~17.4x and P/B of ~1.64x are not statistically cheap; consistent Rs.1.00 DPS in FY2024/FY2025 yields ~2.6% at current price
watch_factors: Operating cash flow was sharply negative this quarter (-Rs.6,820.47mn) on a Rs.8,682.3mn rise in project advances for BESS construction -- a working-capital item to monitor as the build-out continues
The Rs.88.6mn Wind-segment curtailment loss (Cyclone Ditwah) is described as recoverable from the utility under the SPPA, but recovery is not yet confirmed in this filing
Only one interim quarter is on file -- no QoQ trend and no annual report reviewed to corroborate the multi-year capex and margin trajectory

horizon_notes.6m: Next interim result will show whether margin compression (operating margin 42.5% vs 47.7% YoY) stabilizes as new BESS capacity ramps toward full commissioning, and whether the Rs.88.6mn curtailment loss is recovered.
horizon_notes.1y: If BESS revenue scales as capacity fully commissions and finance costs normalize relative to revenue, PAT growth could catch up to the 23%+ revenue growth pace seen this quarter.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on WindForce converting its multi-technology capacity expansion (Wind, Solar, Hydro, BESS) into proportionate earnings growth without a sustained margin squeeze from project debt.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/energy-policy or currency data source in this project to assess long-term Sri Lankan renewable tariff or FX-exposure trends for WindForce's capex program.

interim_updates.note_text: WindForce PLC (WIND) reported Group revenue of Rs.2,620.1mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), up 23.3% YoY from Rs.2,124.0mn, with PAT up 5.1% YoY to Rs.874.6mn from Rs.832.3mn -- revenue growth outpaced profit growth as gross margin narrowed (Direct Cost rose 43% YoY to Rs.(1,159.7)mn, faster than the 23% revenue increase) and net finance cost rose 44% to Rs.(314.5)mn on new project debt. Per the Managing Director's own quarterly commentary (pg.2), Solar generation revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs.813mn (from Rs.578mn) and was the main growth engine, while Wind revenue fell 4% YoY to Rs.935mn (from Rs.977mn) and Hydro fell 11% YoY to Rs.201mn (from Rs.227mn) -- the MD explicitly attributes part of the Wind shortfall to a one-off: 'A revenue loss of LKR 88.6 million was incurred due to curtailment during the quarter,' with discussions initiated with the utility provider to recover this amount under the Standardised Power Purchase Agreement (SPPA). Share of results of equity accounted investee (associates) rose 11% YoY to Rs.176.6mn from Rs.159.2mn, adding to Group PBT on top of the 5% growth in operating-activity profit (Rs.901.5mn from Rs.861.9mn). The new BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) segment -- 130MW/520MWh across 13 sites, all now installed with battery units and transformer stations per the MD's update -- already contributed Rs.149.2mn of segment revenue this quarter per the accounting segmental note (pg.10), ahead of full commissioning.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for WIND in this database, so no prior quarter (e.g. Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column is used. Reconciliation gap flagged: the MD's letter (pg.2) states Solar revenue of LKR 813mn and Hydro revenue of LKR 201mn for the quarter, but the accounting segmental note (pg.10, by operating entity rather than pure technology) shows Solar at Rs.640.0mn and Hydro at Rs.115.8mn -- Wind is the only one of the three that reconciles exactly between the two sources (935.1mn both ways). This filing does not explain the difference; it likely reflects the MD's letter grouping revenue by generation technology across entities differently from the accounting note's by-entity segmentation (e.g. an 'Overseas EPC & Other' or 'Automobile/Other' entity may hold solar or hydro assets not captured under the note's own 'Solar'/'Hydro' columns). The MD's self-consistent, directly-quoted figures (percentage changes match the absolute values given) are used for the narrative here since they are the only technology-level YoY comparison disclosed; the accounting segmental note's entity-level figures were used for cross-checking the Group revenue total only, which both sources agree on (Rs.2,620.1mn).
interim_updates.takeaway: Revenue growth (+23.3% YoY) is real and broad-based across new capacity (BESS already generating Rs.149.2mn this quarter ahead of full commissioning) and Solar output (+41% YoY per the MD's letter), but profit growth lagged well behind revenue (+5.1% YoY) because direct costs grew faster (+43%) and finance costs on new project debt rose 44% YoY to Rs.314.5mn -- this is a capacity-expansion quarter where the P&L has not yet caught up with the capex cycle. The Rs.88.6mn Cyclone Ditwah curtailment loss on the Wind segment, which management says it intends to recover from the utility under the SPPA, is a specific, quantified and potentially reversible drag rather than a structural decline.
operational_highlights: Group revenue up 23.3% YoY to Rs.2,620.1mn (from Rs.2,124.0mn); PAT up 5.1% YoY to Rs.874.6mn (from Rs.832.3mn) -- profit grew more slowly than revenue as gross and finance costs both rose faster than the top line

Per the MD's quarterly letter (pg.2): Solar generation revenue +41% YoY to LKR 813mn (from LKR 578mn); Wind revenue -4% YoY to LKR 935mn (from LKR 977mn); Hydro revenue -11% YoY to LKR 201mn (from LKR 227mn)

MD's letter discloses a specific one-off: 'A revenue loss of LKR 88.6 million was incurred due to curtailment during the quarter' on the Wind segment (linked to force majeure from Cyclone Ditwah, for which an extension to May 2027 was granted on the affected Puttalam wind project) -- WindForce has initiated discussions with the utility to recover this under the SPPA

BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) segment -- 130MW/520MWh across 13 sites, all now installed with battery units and transformer stations -- already generated Rs.149.2mn of segment revenue this quarter per the accounting segmental note (pg.10), ahead of full commissioning

Direct Cost rose 43% YoY to Rs.(1,159.7)mn (vs 23% revenue growth), and net finance cost rose 44% YoY to Rs.(314.5)mn on Rs.314.5mn finance costs (vs Rs.218.5mn) -- both outpacing revenue growth and compressing margins (operating margin 42.5% vs 47.7% a year earlier)
Share of results of equity accounted investee (associates) up 11% YoY to Rs.176.6mn (from Rs.159.2mn), adding to Group PBT

Cash used in operating activities was Rs.(6,820.5)mn this quarter (vs Rs.(711.4)mn a year earlier), driven by a Rs.8,682.3mn increase in trade & other receivables/project advances -- consistent with cash advances for the ongoing BESS construction programme, a working-capital rather than profitability signal
key_drivers: Solar segment revenue growth of 41% YoY (LKR 813mn from LKR 578mn, per the MD's letter) was the largest single revenue growth driver this quarter

A specific, quantified one-off drag on the Wind segment: 'A revenue loss of LKR 88.6 million was incurred due to curtailment during the quarter' (Cyclone Ditwah-related force majeure), which management is pursuing recovery for from the utility under the SPPA -- this explains most of the 4% YoY decline in Wind segment revenue

Direct Cost (+43% YoY) and net finance cost (+44% YoY, to Rs.314.5mn on new project debt funding the BESS build-out) both grew faster than the 23% revenue increase, which is why PAT grew only 5.1% YoY despite strong top-line growth -- a capex-cycle margin squeeze, not a demand problem
